content: The text provided is a list of references from various studies, articles, and systematic reviews related to breastfeeding, child development, maternal health, and associated outcomes. 1. Yokoi A, Takeuchi N, Ekuni D, Morita M conducted a prospective cohort study in a rural area of Japan to investigate the relationship between early childhood caries and attendance at childcare among toddlers. 2. Yonezu T, Yotsuya K, Yakushiji M explored the characteristics of breastfed children who developed nursing caries in their study published in the Bulletin of Tokyo Dental College. 3. Yuan JM, Yu MC, Ross RK, Gao YT, Henderson BE identified risk factors for breast cancer in Chinese women residing in Shanghai in their research published in Cancer Research. 4. Yun BH, Chon SJ, Choi YS, Cho S, Lee BS, Seo SK examined the impact of prolonged breastfeeding on the development of postmenopausal osteoporosis in populations with insufficient calcium and vitamin D intake, as published in Osteoporosis International. 5. Zhang YY, Liu PY, Deng HW analyzed the effects of reproductive and menstrual history on bone mineral density in Chinese women, as detailed in the Journal of Clinical Densitometry. 6. Zhang M, Xie X, Lee AH, Binns CW demonstrated that prolonged lactation reduces the risk of ovarian cancer in Chinese women, as reported in the European Journal of Cancer Prevention. 7. Zhang M, Lee AH, Binns CW investigated reproductive and dietary risk factors for epithelial ovarian cancer in China, as published in Gynecologic Oncology. 8. Zhang Y, Zhou J, Niu F, Donowitz JR, Haque R, Petri Jr WA, Ma JZ characterized early child growth patterns in height-for-age using functional principal component analysis in an urban slum cohort in Bangladesh, as reported in BMC Pediatrics. 9. Zhao M, Wu H, Liang Y, Liu F, Bovet P, Xi B studied the association between breastfeeding and mortality in children under two years of age in Sub-Saharan Africa, as published in Pediatrics. 10. Zheng T, Duan L, Liu Y, Zhang B, Wang Y, Chen Y, Zhang Y, Owens PH found that lactation reduces breast cancer risk in Shandong Province, China, as detailed in the American Journal of Epidemiology. 11. Zheng T, Holford TR, Mayne ST, Owens PH, Zhang Y, Zhang B, Boyle P, Zahm SH conducted a case-control study in Connecticut to examine the relationship between lactation and breast cancer risk, as published in the British Journal of Cancer. 12. Zheng M, Cameron AJ, Birken CS, Keown-Stoneman C, Laws R, Wen LM, Campbell KJ analyzed early infant feeding practices and their impact on BMI trajectories during the first five years of life, as reported in Obesity. 13. Zhong H, Penders J, Shi Z, Ren H, Cai K, Fang C, et al. investigated the influence of early life events and lifestyle on gut microbiota and metabolic phenotypes in young school-age children, as published in Microbiome. 14. Zhou SJ, Baghurst P, Gibson RA, Makrides M found that the home environment, rather than the duration of breastfeeding, predicts the intelligence quotient of children at four years of age, as reported in Nutrition. 15. Zhou H, Wang XL, Ye F, Zeng XL, Wang Y examined the relationship between child feeding practices and malnutrition in seven remote and impoverished counties in China, as published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 16. Ziegler AG, Schmid S, Huber D, Hummel M, Bonifacio E studied the association between early infant feeding and the risk of developing type 1 diabetes-associated autoantibodies, as reported in JAMA. 17. Zielhuis GA, Heuvelmans-Heinen EW, Rach GH, van den Broek P identified environmental risk factors for otitis media with effusion in preschool children, as published in the Scandinavian Journal of Primary Health Care. 18. Zive MM, McKay H, Frank-Spohner GC, Broyles SL, Nelson JA, Nader PR examined infant feeding practices and adiposity in four-year-old Angloand Mexican-Americans, as reported in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 19. The American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP) released a policy statement on breastfeeding, emphasizing its importance for maternal and child health. 20. Aune D, Norat T, Vatten J conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies to assess the maternal risk of type 2 diabetes associated with breastfeeding, as published in Nutrition, Metabolism & Cardiovascular Diseases. 21. Babic A, Sasamoto N, Rosner BA, Tworoger SS, Jordan SJ, Risch HA, et al. explored the association between breastfeeding and ovarian cancer risk, as reported in JAMA Oncology. 22. Belfort MB, Rifas-Shiman SL, Kleinman KP, Guthrie LB, Bellinger DC, Taveras EM, et al. studied the effects of breastfeeding duration and exclusivity on childhood cognition at ages three and seven years, as published in JAMA Pediatrics. 23. Bernard JY, De Agostini M, Forhan A, et al. investigated the relationship between breastfeeding duration and cognitive development at two and three years of age in the EDEN Mother-Child Cohort, as reported in the Journal of Pediatrics. 24. The Maternal and Child Undernutrition Study Group analyzed global and regional exposures to maternal and child undernutrition and their health consequences, as published in The Lancet. 25. Bonifacino E, Schwartz EB, Jun H, Wessel CB, Corbelli JA conducted a systematic review on the effect of lactation on maternal hypertension, as reported in Breastfeeding Medicine. 26. Brennan L, McDonald J, Shlomowit R studied infant feeding practices and chronic child malnutrition in the Indian states of Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh, as published in Economics and Human Biology. 27. Brion A, Khara T, Dolan C examined the similarities and differences between wasting and stunting and their implications for policy and programming, as reported in the Food and Nutrition Bulletin. 28. Caulfield LE, Bentley ME, Ahmed S analyzed the association between prolonged breastfeeding and malnutrition using data from nineteen demographic and health surveys, as published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 29. Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer conducted a collaborative reanalysis of individual data from 47 epidemiological studies in 30 countries to examine the relationship between breastfeeding and breast cancer, as published in The Lancet. 30. Cui L, Xing L, Tian Y, Bao J, Wang L, Xu D, Zhao B, Li W conducted a meta-analysis of observational studies to investigate the association between breastfeeding and early childhood caries, as published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 31. Daniels MC, Adair LS studied the influence of breastfeeding on cognitive development in Filipino children, as reported in the Journal of Nutrition. 32. Dewey KG reviewed the protective effects of breastfeeding against child obesity, as published in the Journal of Human Lactation. 33. The Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee released the 2020 Scientific Report, emphasizing the importance of breastfeeding for maternal and child health. 34. Dieterich CM, Felice JP, O’Sullivan E, Rasmussen KM reviewed the health outcomes of breastfeeding for the mother-infant dyad, as published in Pediatric Clinics of North America. 35. Dogaru CM, Nyffenegger D, Pescatore AM, Spycher BD, Kuehni CE conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the relationship between breastfeeding and childhood asthma, as reported in the American Journal of Epidemiology. 36. Fraser AB, Grimes DA reviewed the effect of lactation on maternal body weight, as published in Obstetrics and Gynecology Survey. 37. Sustained breastfeeding has been shown to have long-term benefits for maternal and child health, as reviewed in Breastfeeding Review. 38. Musilova S, Rada V, Vlkova E, Bunesova V studied the beneficial effects of human milk oligosaccharides on gut microbiota, as published in Beneficial Microbes. 39. Ng’andu NH, Watts TEE examined the relationship between child growth and breastfeeding duration in urban Zambia, as reported in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. 40. Pan H, He Z, Ling L, et al. analyzed reproductive factors and breast cancer risk among BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation carriers, as published in Cancer Epidemiology. 41. Sankar MJ, Sinha B, Chowdhury R, Bhandari N, Taneja S, Martinez J, Bahl R conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on optimal breastfeeding practices and their impact on infant and child mortality, as reported in Acta Paediatrica. 42. Schwarz EB, Ray RM, Stuebe AM, et al. studied the duration of lactation and its association with maternal cardiovascular disease risk factors, as published in Obstetrics and Gynecology. 43. Stuebe AM, Kleinman K, Gillman MW, et al. examined the relationship between lactation duration and maternal metabolism three years postpartum, as reported in the Journal of Women’s Health. 44. Torris C, Bjornnes AK conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the duration of lactation and maternal risk of metabolic syndrome, as published in Nutrients. 45. Victora CG, Horta BL, de Mola CL, Quevedo L, Pinheiro RT, Gigante DP, et al. studied the association between breastfeeding and intelligence, educational attainment, and income at 30 years of age in a Brazilian birth cohort, as published in The Lancet Global Health. 46. WHO released a report on the optimal duration of exclusive breastfeeding, emphasizing its importance for infant health and development. 47. Xiao H, Zhou Q, Niu G, Han G, Zhang Z, Zhang Q, Bai J, Zhu X conducted a dose-response meta-analysis to investigate the association between breastfeeding and osteoporotic hip fractures in women, as published in the Journal of Orthopedic Surgery and Research. 48. Zeng Y, Tang Y, Tang J, Shi J, Zhang L, Zhu T, Xiao D, Qu Y, Mu D conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the association between breastfeeding duration and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children, as published in Nutritional Neuroscience.
